rv.q: This production of In The Continuum directed by Tim Rhoze, who is also Fleetwood-Jourdain’s Producing Artistic Director, is nothing short of a masterpiece.
In the Continuum has likely never been as pertinent.
The effect conveys the shared fear, desperation and expectations imparted by the people around them.

Redman, who is fairly new to Chicago theater, and Fleetwood-Jourdain vet Perry both find the grim humor in these characters and make us see the connections despite their very different life circumstances.
Audience members will easily be engrossed in this powerful production.

cn.t: This powerful two-hander spotlighting HIV-positive Black women on two continents earns praise for its stirring performances and vital subject matter, though the 2005 play shows its age nearly two decades later.
